campus: Campus Arapiles — Calle de Arapiles 14, barrio de Chamberí, Madrid (UNIE page: 'Campus Arapiles ... más de 7.000 m2 se ubica en Chamberí'; 'Modalidad Presencial / Campus Arapiles'). RUCT names the teaching centre as 'Facultad de Ciencias Sociales Aplicadas y de la Comunicación', centre code 28055250, which the UNIE page also prints ('Centro de impartición: Facultad de Ciencias Sociales Aplicadas y de la Comunicación')
university_awarding: Universidad Internacional de la Empresa (UNIE) — a private Spanish university in its own right (Grupo Planeta / Planeta Formación y Universidades). It awards this título in its own name; there is no third-party awarding body. RUCT lists the awarding institution as 'Universidad Internacional de la Empresa'
official_status: máster universitario (OFFICIAL). Registered in RUCT as 'Máster Universitario en Analítica de Negocio / Master in Business Analytics por la Universidad Internacional de la Empresa', estado 'Publicado en B.O.E.', Nivel académico 'Máster - RD 822/2021 (3)', Nivel MECES 3, 60 ECTS (48 obligatorios + 6 prácticas externas + 6 TFM). The UNIE page also links its 'Informe favorable' and 'Verificación positiva' documents
boe_order: Fecha de verificación 11/03/2024; Consejo de Ministros authorisation 17/09/2024; publication of the Acuerdo in BOE 27/09/2024; publication of the plan de estudios in BOE 25/11/2024; Comunidad de Madrid authorisation 13/08/2024; first year of delivery 2024/2025
europe_recognition: EHEA level 7 (Bologna) — academic recognition across the EHEA. This is an official Spanish máster universitario (RUCT 3500236, MECES 3 = EQF 7, RD 822/2021), so it is a second-cycle EHEA qualification, carries a Diploma Supplement as of right and grants doctoral access, and is eligible for public scholarships. That it is awarded by a PRIVATE university makes no difference to this: officiality comes from ANECA verification and RUCT registration, not from public/private ownership. CAVEAT: EHEA academic recognition is not professional recognition of a regulated profession (Directive 2005/36/EC and a separate national process), and recognition abroad still requires the receiving country's own procedure — the EHEA makes it routine, not automatic
tuition_eu_eur: NOT FOUND — UNIE publishes no price for this master anywhere on its own site. The programme page, the 'Admisión y ayudas' page and the 'Becas y ayudas' page carry no figure; the stated route is 'contactando a nuestros asesores'. No primary-sourced tuition figure exists, so none is recorded
tuition_non_eu_eur: NOT FOUND — and specifically, no nationality-differentiated tariff is published either way. There is no evidence of a non-EU surcharge and no evidence of its absence; page silence is NOT FOUND, not 'no surcharge'. (For context on how private Spanish universities usually behave, a single flat rate is common — but UNIE publishes nothing, so this is not recorded as a finding)
tuition_year_of_rates: NOT FOUND — no rates published, so no year can be attached
fees_extra_eur: NOT FOUND as amounts. Two cost-relevant rules ARE published: (1) admission requires payment of a 'reserva de plaza' after a favourable evaluation ('podrás realizar el pago de tu reserva de plaza para asegurarla') — amount not published; (2) UNIE states verbatim that credit recognition does NOT reduce the fee: 'En las enseñanzas de Máster que contemplen la posibilidad de reconocimiento de asignaturas, el alumno deberá abonar el coste total del programa, incluyendo aquellas asignaturas que resulten reconocidas. El reconocimiento de créditos no comportará, en ningún caso, reducción, exención o modificación del importe de la matrícula'
modality: presencial (on-campus). UNIE page: 'Modalidad Presencial / Campus Arapiles / Duración 1 Año / Créditos 60 ECTS'. Evening timetable: the official academic calendars state 'Horario Clases: Lunes a Viernes de 18:00 a 22:00'. 60 places offered
language_of_instruction: Español — UNIE's own programme page states 'Idioma: Español' in its own data block and again in its enquiry form ('Idioma * Español'). DO NOT be misled by the bilingual registered title 'Máster Universitario en Analítica de Negocio / Master in Business Analytics': the declared language of instruction is Spanish. This is a hard filter for a candidate at Spanish A0/A1 targeting September 2027
start_month: April AND October. The April cohort is confirmed from UNIE's own PDF 'Calendario Académico 2026-27* Conv. Abril — Máster Universitario en Analítica de Negocios — Horario Clases: Lunes a Viernes de 18:00 a 22:00'; the October cohort from the parallel PDF 'Calendario Académico 2026-27* Conv. Octubre'. The programme page's headline says 'Comienza en OCT 2026', so the April intake is visible only through the calendar PDF — that is the spring entry this row is about
notes: KEEPING THE TWO UNIE TITLES APART, as the batch instruction requires. This record is the OFFICIAL 'Máster Universitario en Analítica de Negocio / Master in Business Analytics', RUCT 3500236. It is NOT the same animal as UNIE's 'Máster de Formación Permanente en Inteligencia Artificial', which under RD 822/2021 is the modern legal name for a título propio: not ANECA-verified, not in RUCT, not in MECES, outside the EHEA framework, no Diploma Supplement as of right and NO doctoral access. Nothing on this record may be carried across to that one. RUCT 4318468 CHECKED, as instructed, and it is a THIRD distinct title: 'Máster Universitario en Inteligencia Artificial por la Universidad Internacional de la Empresa' — genuinely OFFICIAL (estado 'Publicado en B.O.E.', MECES 3, RD 1393/2007, 60 ECTS = 48 + 6 prácticas + 6 TFM, verificación 30/05/2023, BOE 06/01/2024, plan de estudios BOE 25/11/2024, Madrid authorisation 14/09/2023, taught at UNIE's Escuela Superior de Ingeniería, Ciencia y Tecnología, centre 28056035, non-substantial modification 09/06/2025). So UNIE runs an official MU en Inteligencia Artificial (4318468) AND a separate Máster de Formación Permanente en Inteligencia Artificial (título propio). The similar names are the trap; the register settles it. HINT CHALLENGED AND CONFIRMED: the input's ruct_code_hint 3500236 is correct — confirmed independently on the RUCT detail page, where the registered title, the awarding university, the 60-ECTS structure and the Facultad de Ciencias Sociales Aplicadas y de la Comunicación all match the UNIE page. COMPLEMENTOS DE FORMACIÓN — THE 300-ECTS / ENGINEERING QUESTION, and a genuine divergence between the two sources. RUCT publishes 'Nº Créditos Complementos Formativos: 0' at TITLE level. But UNIE's own 'Perfil de ingreso' PDF imposes them at APPLICANT level, and it names this candidate's exact case: the master is aimed at graduates in ADE, Marketing, Negocios Internacionales, Analítica de Negocios and Economía, and states that applicants from other backgrounds 'deberán cursar los complementos formativos ... Estos complementos formativos tendrán carácter obligatorio, y se realizarán antes del primer semestre del máster'. Its table maps 'Grados o licenciaturas del ámbito de la Ingeniería y Arquitectura ... sin formación previa en organizaciones de empresas dentro de su plan de estudios' to the complemento 'Organización y Administración de empresas'. A Software Engineering graduate therefore faces at least one compulsory bridging module BEFORE the first semester unless their transcript shows business-organisation content. This is exactly the RUCT-0-is-not-the-whole-answer case the AGENT-BRIEF warns about, and it is recorded here as the applicant-level rule, distinct from the title-level 0. AND the 300 ECTS do NOT buy relief on price: UNIE states that recognised subjects are still charged at the full programme cost. ADMISSION also includes a test: 'Realizarás una prueba tipo test que se compone de tres partes: evaluación de competencias y actitudes hacia el trabajo intelectual, inglés y valoración de méritos.' TUITION: recorded NOT FOUND deliberately. Aggregators quote figures for this programme; none is sourceable on a UNIE page, and per the non-negotiable rules an unsourced fee is a corrupted record. A human should ask UNIE admissions ([email protected] / +34 919 032 201) for the 2027-28 tariff and whether any non-EU differential applies.

europe_recognition: EHEA level 7 (Bologna) — academic recognition across the EHEA. Being a private, fully online university does not weaken this: officiality comes from ANECA verification and RUCT registration. UNIR's ESIT additionally holds an ANECA AUDIT quality seal. institution: Harbour.Space Institute of Technology, Barcelona — INTERNATIONAL BRANCH-STYLE PRIVATE INSTITUTE operating in Spain (sister campus in Bangkok)
programme_name: Master's in Applied Computer Data Science; also Master's in Computer Science, Data Science, Cyber Security (Barcelona campus)
campus: Harbour Space Institute of Technology, Carrer de Rosa Sensat 9-11, 08005 Barcelona (Poblenou / 22@ district) — address published on Harbour.Space's own About page. A second campus operates in Bangkok at UTCC; the page offers a semester there for 'a second accredited diploma', which is a Thai qualification, not a Spanish one
university_awarding: NONE — no university awards this. Harbour.Space is not a university and awards the diploma itself: the programme page states 'Graduate with a Harbour.Space diploma shaped by industry' and labels the award 'Master of Engineering · 90 ECTS'. That is a private institute certificate, not a Spanish título. A UVic-UCC double diploma exists only for 'specific programmes' and only as an 'opportunity' (Harbour.Space's own hedged wording) — and CRITICALLY, the page for THIS programme does not mention UVic-UCC anywhere at all (zero occurrences in the fetched page). So for this master, no Spanish university is named as awarding anything. If a candidate wants the UVic-UCC route they must get Harbour.Space to name, in writing, the exact official UVic-UCC título, its RUCT code, and the conditions
institution_type: private school (not a university). Harbour.Space describes itself as 'an acknowledged educational institution in Spain with an authorised Spanish license of 08078491' — a centre licence number, not university status. It is absent from RUCT (a direct RUCT query for 'harbour' returns zero rows), which is expected because RUCT registers universities, their centres and their official titles, and Harbour.Space is none of those in respect of this master. It is not one of Spain's recognised universities and cannot issue a título universitario oficial
official_status: NOT an official Spanish title — título propio-equivalent at best, and arguably not even that, since a título propio is issued by a Spanish university and this is issued by a non-university institute. NOT ANECA-verified. NOT in RUCT. No BOE verification or authorisation. The award is a Harbour.Space 'Master of Engineering' diploma of 90 ECTS. Do not read Harbour.Space's word 'accredited' as meaning ANECA/RUCT accreditation: in its own FAQ the word attaches to the PARTNER universities' diplomas (UVic-UCC, UTCC), not to the Harbour.Space diploma
boe_order: NONE — no BOE verification, authorisation or homologation order exists for this award. (For contrast, this is also not the Enseñanzas Artísticas case, where RUCT absence is expected and a BOE homologation order supplies the evidence instead; here there is no such order and no separate official register)
meces_level: NOT IN MECES — the qualification is not in the Spanish qualifications framework at any level
eqf_level: NOT IN EQF via Spain — Spain has referenced MECES to the EQF, so a qualification outside MECES has no Spanish route to an EQF level. Any EQF claim would have to come from another country's framework and none is evidenced
europe_recognition: NO AUTOMATIC ACADEMIC RECOGNITION IN EUROPE. This is BRIEF case (c). The award is a private institute's own certificate: it is not in MECES, not inside the EHEA/Bologna qualifications framework, carries no Diploma Supplement as of right, and grants no doctoral access in Spain or elsewhere. It uses ECTS and Harbour.Space markets 'accreditation', but ECTS is a credit-counting convention, not a recognition mechanism, and neither ECTS nor a Spanish centre licence puts a qualification into the EHEA. Recognition is at the sole discretion of the receiving institution or employer, case by case. Harbour.Space says this itself, and its own words are the clearest evidence on the record: 'While we have successfully achieved these accreditation milestones through our partnerships, we continue to align all our courses with the European Credit Transfer System (ECTS), ensuring recognition by our partner institutions' — i.e. recognition by PARTNERS, not generally — and 'Should you have any concerns or specific requirements for recognition, we are prepared to liaise directly with the relevant institutions to establish one-to-one agreements tailored to your needs.' A qualification whose recognition has to be negotiated one institution at a time is by definition not automatically recognised. CONSEQUENCES FOR THIS CANDIDATE, stated plainly and not softened: no PhD access on the strength of this degree; no eligibility for Spanish public postgraduate scholarships (FPU/FPI, MEC becas) which require an official título; no automatic second-cycle standing in any other EHEA country; and Spanish homologación/equivalencia of the award is not available because the award is not an official Spanish qualification to begin with. The only route to an EHEA-recognised second-cycle qualification here is the UVic-UCC double diploma, which is not offered on this programme's page and would have to be confirmed in writing, with a RUCT code, before it could be relied on. NOTE the standard caveat cuts the other way too: even a genuinely official Spanish master would need the receiving country's own procedure abroad — the EHEA makes recognition routine, not automatic. Here there is no EHEA standing to start from
diploma_supplement: NO — not as of right. A Diploma Supplement (Suplemento Europeo al Título) is an entitlement attached to official Spanish títulos; this award is not one. Nothing on Harbour.Space's site offers one
phd_access: NO — doctoral access in Spain requires an official máster universitario (or an equivalent recognised qualification giving 300 ECTS of official study). This award confers no such access. Note the candidate would separately have a stronger PhD-access position from their existing 300-ECTS Tunisian engineering degree than from adding this diploma
tuition_eu_eur: EUR 22,900 for the full 1-year, 90-ECTS master — 'Master 22.900€ / Tuition for International Students' on the programme page. IMPORTANT: the discount axis is CITIZENSHIP, not EU/non-EU. Harbour.Space's fees FAQ states 'Spanish and Thai students benefit from a 50% discount on any tuition fee', which implies EUR 11,450 for a Spanish or Thai citizen; the programme page shows the same as a 'Spanish citizens −50%' tab. A non-Spanish EU citizen therefore pays the same EUR 22,900 as anyone else. Only the 22,900 figure is actually printed as a number; the 11,450 is the arithmetic consequence of the stated 50% (22,900 x 0.5 = 11,450) and is flagged as derived, not printed
tuition_non_eu_eur: EUR 22,900 — the same figure. THIS is the rate this Tunisian candidate pays: no non-EU surcharge, but also no discount, because the 50% reduction is reserved for Spanish and Thai citizens. Flat single international rate, explicitly stated as such. (Harbour.Space's FAQ gives the institute-wide band: 'full study programmes cost between 3500€ and 22,900€, depending on programme type and duration'; this master sits at the top of that band)
tuition_year_of_rates: Rates as published on harbour.space on 2026-08-29, for intakes running in 2026 (site footer '© 2026', schedule page 'Schedule 2026'). Harbour.Space does not label its prices by academic year, so no academic-year label can honestly be attached; a 2027-28 figure is NOT published
fees_extra_eur: EUR 125 non-refundable application fee, required for all programmes ('a small application fee of 125€ is required for all programmes, and is non-refundable'; the programme page repeats '+€125 application fee'). Harbour.Space states that learning materials, out-of-class excursions and living costs are NOT included in tuition. No other compulsory fee is published. Discounts of 'up to 50% off tuition' and company sponsorship ('25% of students have their tuition fully covered by a company') are advertised but not quantified per applicant
modality: presencial (on-campus, Barcelona). Structure: 1 year, 90 ECTS, delivered as 14 focused three-week modules, roughly half core and half electives, ending in a Capstone Project. Full-time
language_of_instruction: English — the programme page states 'Language: English'. All application material must be submitted in English, and non-English diplomas need certified English translations. This is the ONE field on which this option beats most of the Spanish public and private alternatives for a candidate at Spanish A0/A1
start_month: Continuous — a new module intake roughly every 3 weeks, all year. Harbour.Space states verbatim: 'Intake every 3 weeks! There is no "application deadline" — you can start any upcoming module!' and the programme page's own field reads 'Starts: Every 3 weeks'. So a spring 2027 start and a September 2027 start are both possible; there is no cohort structure to miss
notes: THE BATCH TRAP, ANSWERED FROM SOURCE. Harbour.Space is not a Spanish university and this degree is NOT a Spanish official título. What it actually awards, checked on its own pages: a Harbour.Space 'Master of Engineering' diploma of 90 ECTS, under its own authority. Its claimed standing is 'an authorised Spanish license of 08078491' — that is a Spanish education-CENTRE licence number, not university recognition and not title verification; note the number's shape matches the eight-digit Catalan centre codes RUCT itself uses for teaching centres (e.g. UPC's ESEIAAT is 08072671), i.e. it identifies a registered centre, not an accredited degree. A direct RUCT query for 'harbour' returns zero rows. MARKETING LANGUAGE REJECTED AS EVIDENCE, as instructed. Three specific phrases were tested and none of them supports a MECES/EQF claim: (1) 'acknowledged educational institution' — not a legal category; (2) 'accredited degree from ... UVic-UCC' — the accreditation belongs to UVic-UCC's own title, not to the Harbour.Space diploma, and it is offered only for 'specific programmes' and only as an 'opportunity' (Harbour.Space's own hedges, quoted in the batch input and confirmed verbatim on the live FAQ today); (3) 'aligned with ECTS ... ensuring recognition by our partner institutions' — recognition by named partners is the opposite of general recognition. Its own closing offer to 'liaise directly with the relevant institutions to establish one-to-one agreements' is a concession that recognition is bespoke. THE UVIC-UCC ROUTE DOES NOT APPEAR ON THIS PROGRAMME AT ALL. The fetched page for Master's in Applied Data and Computer Science contains ZERO mentions of UVic, Vic, or Central University of Catalonia. The only second diploma it offers is Thai (UTCC, via a Bangkok semester). Nor does UVic-UCC appear in output/ruct-backbone.jsonl with any official master matching this subject area (its registered masters in the nine fields are Health Data Science, Omics Data Analysis, Biomedical Data Science, Gestión Empresarial, Dirección Integral de Negocios). So there is no identified official Spanish title behind this programme. Anyone relying on the double-diploma claim must obtain, in writing, the exact UVic-UCC título name and its RUCT code. PROGRAMME NAME MISMATCH, flagged as required. The input's programme_name is 'Master's in Applied Computer Data Science; also Master's in Computer Science, Data Science, Cyber Security (Barcelona campus)'. The live page at the input's own URL is titled 'Master's in Applied Data and Computer Science' (word order differs) and covers only that one master; the other three named in the input string are separate Harbour.Space masters. The input string is echoed VERBATIM as instructed so the join key survives; this note records the discrepancy. All facts on this record come from the Applied Data and Computer Science page plus institute-wide pages (About, FAQ, Admissions), and the fee band, application fee, citizenship discount, licence claim and recognition wording are institute-wide and therefore apply to the sibling masters too. WHAT IT IS GOOD FOR. English-taught, rolling three-weekly intakes with no deadline, one year, strong industry-practitioner faculty and a Barcelona location. For a candidate whose blocker is Spanish-language instruction, that is a genuine advantage. But at EUR 22,900 with no non-EU discount, no MECES level, no Diploma Supplement, no PhD access and no public-scholarship eligibility, it is the weakest option in this batch on every criterion the candidate ranked as decisive except language and start-date flexibility. ONE ADJACENT FACT, not to be confused with the above: Harbour.Space also advertises 'FP Grado Superior' provision. Spanish FP is a separate official system (LOE/LOMLOE) with its own register, and nothing on this record about the master's status should be read across to those programmes, which were not investigated here.
